---
title: "Install everything needed for the SAM fire mapping app"
output: html_document
---

This document installs the R packages, the Python packages (PyTorch and SAM2) and the SAM2 model weights needed to run `app-sam-fire`. You need to have python installed and know paste the path in below. Its best not to install the most recent python version because some python packages need a slightly older version (e.g. PyTorch).

**How to use it:** open this file in RStudio, check the settings in the first chunk, then click **Run All** (Ctrl+Alt+R) or **Knit**. It takes 10–30 minutes the first time, mostly downloading PyTorch and the model weights.

**Start from a fresh R session** (Session → Restart R). Once R has connected to a Python, it can't switch to another one, so the Python setup below only works in a session that hasn't used Python yet.

# 1. Settings

Change these if needed. The defaults work for most people.

```{r settings}
# Path to an existing Python 3.10-3.12 executable, e.g.
#   Windows: "C:/Users/me/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python311/python.exe"
#   Mac/Linux: "/usr/bin/python3"
# Leave as NULL to find an installed Python automatically (section 3 explains what to do if none is found).
python_path <- NULL

# Name of the Python virtual environment to create for SAM2.
envname <- "sam2_env"

# PyTorch build:
#   "cpu"   - works on any computer (slower segmentation)
#   "cu126" - NVIDIA GPU with a recent driver (check with `nvidia-smi`; "cu124" or "cu118" for older drivers)
# Ignored on macOS, where the standard build is used (it supports Apple Silicon GPUs).
torch_build <- "cpu"

# Folder for the SAM2 model weights (~300 MB for the default Base+ model).
checkpoints_dir <- file.path(path.expand("~"), "sam2", "checkpoints")

# Writable working folder the app uses for temporary files.
wk_dir <- file.path(path.expand("~"), "sam2", "wk_dir")
```

```{r setup-options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
# Large downloads (PyTorch, model weights) need longer than R's default 60 s timeout.
options(timeout = 3600)
```

# 2. R packages

Installs any of the app's R packages that are missing, then the `fireobs` package from GitHub.

```{r r-packages}
cran_pkgs <- c(
  "shiny", "leaflet", "leaflet.extras", "sortable", "leafem", "terra", "sf",
  "dplyr", "smoothr", "bsplus", "geojsonsf", "jsonlite", "lwgeom", "nngeo",
  "units", "purrr", "glue", "magick", "reticulate", "remotes"
)

missing_pkgs <- cran_pkgs[!vapply(cran_pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]

if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  message("Installing: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
  install.packages(missing_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
} else {
  message("All CRAN packages already installed.")
}

remotes::install_github("mstorey87/fireobs", upgrade = "never")

still_missing <- c(cran_pkgs, "fireobs")[
  !vapply(c(cran_pkgs, "fireobs"), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(still_missing) > 0) {
  stop("These R packages failed to install: ", paste(still_missing, collapse = ", "),
       "\nScroll up for the error messages.")
}
```

# 3. Python

Uses `python_path` if you set one. Otherwise it looks for an installed Python 3.10–3.12. SAM2 needs Python 3.10 or newer.

> **Note:** avoid the newest Python release. PyTorch, OpenCV and other packages often take a few months to support a new Python version, so the install can fail with errors like "no matching distribution found for torch". If that happens, install an older Python (3.11 or 3.12 are safe choices) and use that instead.

If none is found, install Python yourself:

1. Download Python 3.11 from <https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3119/> ("Windows installer (64-bit)" on Windows, or the macOS installer). On Ubuntu/Debian, run `sudo apt install python3 python3-venv` instead.
2. Run the installer with the default options.
3. Find the path to `python.exe` (Windows) or `python3` (Mac/Linux). On Windows it is usually `C:/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python311/python.exe`.
4. Run this chunk again and paste that path when asked, or set `python_path` in the settings chunk.

```{r python}
library(reticulate)

no_python_msg <- paste0(
  "No Python 3.10-3.12 was found.\n",
  "Install Python 3.11 from https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3119/ ",
  "(Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt install python3 python3-venv),\n",
  "then set python_path in the settings chunk to the path of python.exe / python3 and run again."
)

if (is.null(python_path)) {
  python_path <- reticulate::virtualenv_starter(">=3.10,<3.13")
}

if (is.null(python_path)) {
  if (interactive()) {
    message(no_python_msg)
    python_path <- trimws(readline("Or paste the path to python.exe / python3 here (blank to stop): "), whitespace = "[\\s\"']")
    if (!nzchar(python_path)) stop("No Python path given.")
  } else {
    stop(no_python_msg)
  }
}

if (!file.exists(python_path)) stop("Python not found at: ", python_path)
message("Using Python: ", python_path)
system2(python_path, "--version")
```

# 4. Python virtual environment and packages

Creates a separate virtual environment so SAM2 and PyTorch don't interfere with any other Python projects.

```{r python-env}
if (!reticulate::virtualenv_exists(envname)) {
  reticulate::virtualenv_create(envname, python = python_path,
                                packages = c("pip", "setuptools", "wheel", "numpy"))
} else {
  message("Virtual environment '", envname, "' already exists - reusing it.")
}

# PyTorch. Windows and Linux need an explicit index to get the CPU or the matching CUDA build.
torch_pip_options <- if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Darwin") {
  character()
} else {
  c("--index-url", paste0("https://download.pytorch.org/whl/", torch_build))
}
reticulate::virtualenv_install(envname, c("torch", "torchvision"),
                               pip_options = torch_pip_options)

reticulate::virtualenv_install(envname, "opencv-python-headless")

# SAM2's own dependencies (from its setup.py).
reticulate::virtualenv_install(envname, c("tqdm", "hydra-core", "iopath", "pillow"))

# SAM2 itself is plain Python (its only compiled part is an optional GPU extension), so rather than
# building it with pip, its source folder is downloaded from GitHub and copied into the environment.
sam2_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "sam2-main.zip")
download.file("https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2/archive/refs/heads/main.zip",
              sam2_zip, mode = "wb")
unzip(sam2_zip, exdir = tempdir())

venv_python <- reticulate::virtualenv_python(envname)
site_packages <- system2(venv_python,
                         c("-c", shQuote("import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_paths()['purelib'])")),
                         stdout = TRUE)
unlink(file.path(site_packages, "sam2"), recursive = TRUE)
ok <- file.copy(file.path(tempdir(), "sam2-main", "sam2"), site_packages, recursive = TRUE)
if (!ok) stop("Couldn't copy SAM2 into ", site_packages)
message("SAM2 copied to ", file.path(site_packages, "sam2"))
```

# 5. Check the Python setup

```{r python-check}
reticulate::use_virtualenv(envname, required = TRUE)

torch <- reticulate::import("torch")
reticulate::import("sam2")
reticulate::import("cv2")

message("PyTorch version: ", torch$`__version__`)
message("GPU (CUDA) available: ", torch$cuda$is_available())
if (torch_build != "cpu" && !torch$cuda$is_available()) {
  warning("A GPU build of PyTorch was requested but no GPU was detected - ",
          "SAM2 will run on the CPU. Check your NVIDIA driver with `nvidia-smi`.")
}
```

# 6. Download the model weights and test SAM2

`fire_load_sam_once()` downloads the checkpoint and config into `checkpoints_dir` if they aren't already there, then loads the model. If this chunk finishes without an error, the app is ready to run.

```{r sam-check}
dir.create(checkpoints_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(wk_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

fireobs:::fire_load_sam_once(
  checkpoints_dir,
  pt_name   = "sam2.1_hiera_base_plus.pt",
  yaml_name = "sam2.1_hiera_b+.yaml"
)
```

# 7. Point the app at this setup

Replace the setup lines near the top of `app.R` (the `reticulate::use_python(...)`, `wk_dir` and `chkp_dir` lines) with the lines printed below:

```{r app-config, echo = FALSE}
venv_python <- normalizePath(reticulate::virtualenv_python(envname), winslash = "/")
cat(sprintf(
'reticulate::use_python("%s", required = TRUE)
wk_dir   <- "%s"
chkp_dir <- "%s"
',
  venv_python,
  normalizePath(wk_dir, winslash = "/"),
  normalizePath(checkpoints_dir, winslash = "/")
))
```

Then start the app with the command printed below. It uses the full path to the app folder (the folder this file is in), so it works whatever R's working directory is. You can also open `app.R` in RStudio and click **Run App**.

```{r run-command, echo = FALSE}
cat(sprintf('shiny::runApp("%s")\n', normalizePath(".", winslash = "/")))
```
